correctness.rationale: The stationary recurrence is a strict contraction on differences of states and gives the stated geometric series. In an eigenbasis its Hilbert–Schmidt norm squared gives the kernel z/(z+a); summing within degenerate eigenspaces makes the masses basis independent. Positive masses imply the strict derivative signs for m>0, while m=0 gives constant purity 1. Since p maps bijectively to z>0, the 2m cross-multiplied equations use distinct nodes off the poles. The difference of two candidate cross products has degree at most 2m−1, and the true numerator is coprime to the true monic denominator, so even a candidate with a common factor cannot create an extra solution. Residues give the positive-gap masses and normalization gives B0. Independently counted circular differences modulo 36 for the listed sets, and enumerated rotations and reflected rotations: the signed count arrays agree and no congruence maps the sets. This is an exact-data sufficiency result, not minimality or stability. RESULT.md:26–55 is the analytic replay; the frozen verify.py was inspected, not run. Its reported finite checks do not certify the theorem.
